Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by the claimant on this one, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane road in Katy, Texas, right near a shopping center entrance. I was trying to move over one
lane to make my turn.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I had my signal on and I checked my mirror. I didn't see anything in the lane next to me, so I started drifting over
slowly. Then I heard a loud bang on my passenger side and felt my car get pushed.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before contact?
A: Not really. I think it was there in my blind spot. I didn't catch it until the moment we touched.
Q: How fast were you going?
A: I'd say maybe thirty-five, forty. Traffic was moving but not heavy.
Q: Did you stop after the impact, and did you speak with the other driver?
A: Yes, I pulled over onto the shoulder. The other driver got out and we talked briefly. He said he didn't see me either.
Q: Were you hurt at the scene?
A: My neck felt stiff, but I thought I'd just be sore. By the next morning I had headaches and sharp pain running into
my shoulders. I went to urgent care and they diagnosed whiplash.
Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I'm doing physical therpay twice a week and I still can't turn my head fully to the left without pain.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to get this resolved so I can get back to normal, and I'm willing to provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
